A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Metropolis-Hastings framework for 3D Gaussian reconstruction. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, convergence measurements, and component and relocation ablations on three benchmark datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains those original benchmark results and adds time-to-target measurements and experiments isolating the sampling algorithm and importance scores.

M1.justification: The loss, multi-view importance computation, coarse/fine proposals, voxel-dependent acceptance rule, relocation, and optimization pipeline remain unchanged. The new sampler-only and no-importance experiments are ablations, not modifications to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate novel-view synthesis on the same nine Mip-NeRF360 scenes, two Tanks and Temples scenes, and two Deep Blending scenes. The additional experiments introduce no new dataset, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator set is unchanged. v2 Table 4 adds a comparison of stripped-down 3DGS+MH and 3DGS+SGLD implementations. The aggregate relocation comparison drops the unrestricted 3DGS row from v1 Table 7; its retained count-matched 3DGS-S comparator is simply renamed 3DGS.

E3.justification: v2 supplements the existing convergence evaluation with wall-clock time to fixed PSNR targets of 21, 24, 27, and 30 dB. It also introduces a sampler-only comparison at matched 0.85-million Gaussian counts. Existing benchmark metrics and stated training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Tables 4–5 substantially extend component attribution by directly comparing core MH and SGLD sampling and removing the entire importance-score mechanism. v1 tested individual score cues and relocation but lacked these controls. Existing aggregate ablations are retained, while some scene-specific ablation breakdowns disappear.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments continue the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores, per-scene results, and Gaussian-count tables are numerically unchanged. v2 adds timing and sampler-ablation results; for example, Table 1 reports reaching 30 dB in 851.52 seconds versus 983.05 seconds for 3DGS-MCMC. Some scene-specific ablation entries from v1 Tables 2–3 are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Appendix A–C derivations are unchanged apart from numbering and wording. The standard MH acceptance and detailed-balance equations move from v1 Appendix F to v2 Section 3.2; they are not new theoretical contributions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim adaptive probabilistic density control, fewer Gaussians with competitive reconstruction quality, and faster convergence. Faster convergence was already an explicit contribution in v1. v2 emphasizes and adds evidence for these retained claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets the sampling mechanism as the primary source of performance, with multi-view importance scores providing guidance, based on the added ablations. The limitations concerning sparse outdoor scenes and approximately five minutes of photometric-error overhead remain; proposed future remedies become more specific.

D1.justification: The implementation basis, RTX 3090 hardware, stated 30K-iteration budget, proposal scales, voxel sizes, batch sizes, and pseudocode are retained. Project-page and dataset-access disclosures also remain. The added experiments provide no substantive new implementation instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Efficient Density Control, Speedy-Splat, and PUP 3D-GS, including discussion of deterministic geometric splitting. It removes GIRAFFE, pixelNeRF, and DreamScene360 references while condensing related work. The principal positioning against 3DGS-MCMC remains unchanged; the newly cited methods are not evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: v2 merges and condenses related-work subsections, moves the MH primer into Section 3.2, incorporates appendix ablations into the main text, and reorganizes the remaining appendices. It also edits prose, adds acknowledgments, and updates the publication header, while retaining the overall narrative and method structure.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially reorganized: v2 adds a coarse/fine proposal visualization, timing table, and sampler-comparison table; promotes aggregate appendix ablations into main-text Tables 3 and 5; and removes the small scene-specific ablation tables. The convergence plot is repositioned and enlarged, while its image and the qualitative reconstruction image remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added matched-count sampler comparison, no-importance ablation, and time-to-target table strengthen evidence for claims that v1 supported less directly. Moving the MH background and aggregate ablations into the main text also improves accessibility. These gains are limited by the loss of scene-specific ablation detail and mixed SSIM/LPIPS outcomes in Table 4, which warrant caution about the broad superiority interpretation.
